calls.head: Like for like: Miller against Guentzel
calls.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Miller’s line (Miller, Kartye and Lafrenière) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Lightning’s second line is Guentzel, Cirelli and Hagel.

calls.nums: At home: 39% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against second lines, about 29% with no line matching

surprises.head: The Rangers brought the hits
surprises.body: The Rangers are one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Even by those standards, this was a lot of hitting: a hit score of 211 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 119 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: The Rangers beat the Lightning
paras: Alexis Lafrenière got the scoring started for the Rangers 1:02 in. Lafrenière scored his second of the night midway through the first to make it 2-0. Zemgus Girgensons got the Lightning on the board 4:39 later. Will Cuylle made it 3-1 for the Rangers late in the second. Mika Zibanejad added an empty-net goal with 2:44 left to make it 4-1.
The chances were closer than the score. Dylan Garand made 25 saves for the Rangers, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 19 of 22. By our Swing measure, Marcus Pettersson had the best night of anyone.
Jeffrey Viel and Matt Rempe fought late in the first. The Rangers killed all four Lightning power plays. The Rangers improved to 6-2-0, and the Lightning dropped to 4-2-0.

items.text: The Lightning’s four-game winning streak is over.
Mika Zibanejad extended his point streak against Tampa Bay to seven games.
Nikita Kucherov’s five-game point streak ended.
Zemgus Girgensons scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 2 (eleven games played since).
